$comment: The web↔FACE mapping, and the only place the rename lives.
`face` is the exact Dart field name in runink_theme.dart, so drift is detectable
(check-face-parity.mjs). `web` is a SEMANTIC ROLE — hues are deliberately not in
the name, so a palette re-tune does not force a rename across 54 components.
`positions` is the load-bearing field. Each entry becomes a key in exactly those
Tailwind theme palettes and no others, which is what makes misuse fail to compile
rather than fail to be legible: a fill has no textColor entry, so `text-fill-success`
does not exist. FACE enforces the same rule with a test suite; the web enforces it
with the type of the utility.
Tiers are the WCAG floors, which is why they are stable:
fill — no foreground position at all. Below 3:1 as ink on its own surfaces.
mark — ≥3:1. Borders, rings, icons. Never text.
ink  — ≥4.5:1 as text on all four surfaces of its ramp.

surfaces.why: The page. Warm near-black on console, warm paper on sheet. The FACE name is misleading on the web (it is *light* in the sheet ramp) which is exactly why the web name is a role.

The default card. NOTE: in the sheet ramp this goes *lighter* than the canvas (#FFFDFA on #FBF7F1) while surface-raised and surface-well go darker — so these four are NOT a depth ladder and must not be renamed raised-1/2/3.
The warm/tan panel. FACE's GlassCard fill.

surfaceHighlight under a second name because the border rule differs from the surface rule. Valid over canvas/surface/surface-raised only — over surface-well it is the same value, so the border vanishes. Use `edge` there.

FACE has no ≥3:1 boundary token; origin/main did (--rk-rule-strong). Expressed as an alpha on textPrimary rather than a new hex, so it survives a FACE re-tune. Measured 3.41/3.38/3.31/3.15 console, 3.46/3.50/3.40/3.25 sheet.

inks.why: Titles and body. `text-primary` is a TEXT ROLE — there is no `primary` colour family any more and one must not be reintroduced.

Labels and secondary text. Carries a real alpha that DIFFERS per ramp on purpose (0x99 console, 0xB3 sheet) — dark ink on a light ground needs more opacity for the same ratio. Because the alpha is baked, the Tailwind /NN modifier does nothing useful here; check-usage.mjs bans it.
The compliant accent ink. Its SHEET value (#8B4024) is DARK — this token is not 'a lighter orange'. Not inkable by on-accent.
The ONLY olive that may carry text or a small mark.
The provenance hue as ink — AI-generated tag, BLOCKED verdict, anomaly count.
One of FACE's two cool mark families.

fills.why: Primary accent (terracotta). A mark, NOT text: in the sheet ramp it measures 3.62/3.81/3.39/3.02 on the four surfaces, under the 4.5 text floor. Focus rings over surface-well in the sheet ramp sit at 3.02 — zero headroom, so pair with a 1px ink offset.

A FILL. Never ink — 2.97/2.69/2.55/2.20 as a foreground on the console surfaces, below even the 3:1 mark floor. Keeps its own wash tone so a critical/high severity chip stays distinct from an accent-washed one.
Top stop of the brand gradient, split off from technicalOrangeLight on purpose so the ink could darken without flattening the gradient.
Success (olive) — a fill. Sets the wash-alpha ceiling: the light olive pair measures 4.64 at 0.15 and 4.44 at 0.18.
Info/secondary olive; the default GlassCard glow. A fill.
Secondary (wine) — a fill. FACE is explicit that Reject is wine, not red; do not respecify it as red.

onFills.why: The ink for anything ON a technicalOrange fill. Near-black in BOTH ramps — the one token that does not flip. NOT valid on ink-accent (2.44).
Solid olive fill + family ink would be 1.00:1 in the sheet ramp (oliveInk == oliveSuccess there). This closes that. 6.17 in both ramps. A plain const because the fill it inks does not flip.

$comment: Its own family, disjoint from every brand name. FACE: 'do not colour a status
with accent/olive/wine.' There is deliberately NO solid severity fill — all five
bands share one wash, because a wash at 0.15 carries only 15% of the difference
between two tones, which is how five 'different' chips once ended up 1.047:1 apart.
Colour is NOT sufficient here and the component API must enforce it: adjacent bands
cannot be pushed past ~1.17:1 in this ramp, so every severity indicator also carries
a glyph or the word. A bare text-ink-severity-* span is a usage-checker finding.

wash.why: A FILL. Never ink. The ONE shared ground for every severity chip.

knownCollisions: console severityHigh is dE 0.045 from ink-accent
console severityCritical is dE 0.058 from ink-provenance
A severity mark beside an accent or provenance mark will not read as a different family on hue alone. The glyph disambiguates.
